headline: Shout orders at the gravel yard — and the crew obeys
lede: GRAVEL YARD learned to listen: press V (or tap the MIC pill) and the CPU crew takes dictation — gate settings, batch starts, and delivery pins, in the yard's own radio words. A never-dry pick closed the title's oldest honest gap; the sim stays pure pads underneath.

notes.text: Five voice orders with honest refusals: GATE WIDE/MEDIUM/NARROW, RUN IT, JOG IT, PIN COARSE/FINES, PIN CLEAR. The truck really walks to the order board and cycles the pin; the operator sets the gate against the demand chart — one-shot overrides, not policy.

Laws kept: orders end in pads, voice is solo-local (net play refuses), the order queue is never hashed — full-CPU reference runs stay bit-identical, and the recording path banks calls only with the voice consent grant.

gravelcheck grew to 131 Node gates (+35 voice gates incl. determinism same-shouts/identical-hash and shouted-vs-silent divergence) plus 5 headless browser gates; stubbing the pin-retire line goes exactly one gate red.
Pick provenance: weakest-stage honesty — MAGIC CARPET scored higher but its gaps are all owned by live QA pass #1764, so the lane took GRAVEL YARD's oldest unowned gap instead.
